destination.name: Echuca
destination.tagline: A Murray River port where paddle steamers still sail from the historic wharf
destination.description: Echuca sits on the Murray River, with the New South Wales town of Moama opposite, and has 15,056 people. Its port is home to the largest paddle steamer fleet in the world, including PS Adelaide (1866), the world's oldest operating wooden-hulled paddle steamer. PS Pevensey (1911) and PS Alexander Arbuthnot (1923) sail commercially from the port daily. Echuca is about 2.5 hours' drive from Melbourne.
whyVisit: Cruise the Murray on a paddle steamer

goodToKnow.title: Sit in the front carriages
goodToKnow.detail: On the train from Melbourne, sit in the front 3 cars, as the rear 3 decouple at Bendigo.

goodToKnow.title: Easy to walk around
goodToKnow.detail: Apart from occasional buses there is no town transport, but the town is small enough to walk.

goodToKnow.title: Southern 80 in February
goodToKnow.detail: February brings the Southern 80 waterski race and a music festival, so expect busy river banks and book ahead.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months} for river cruises without the February Southern 80 crowds.

notes: Sources give no best-time guidance; spring and autumn inferred. The Barmah forest reason is generalised from the researcher's experiences list.
